_game: Rush Hour (puzzle: slide cars to free the red car)
_note: Setup: the `rushhour` extra (rushhour-gym>=0.6.0). On first use the package downloads the rushhour-env Go engine of the matching Rush-Hour release into ~/.cache/rushhour-gym/ (checksum-verified); set RUSHHOUR_ENV_BIN or the phase 'binary' field to use a binary of your own. The env is RushHourHuman-v0: the Rush-Hour program's own interface (button selection, its picture, its trial flow, its results columns in info), all in the package -- the adapter is a keymap plus the fields to log.
_keys_note: Env action space Discrete(8) = rushinput's meta-actions: 0..3 choose the car up/down/left/right (spatial, what Rush-Hour's gamepad d-pad does), 4/5 choose the previous/next car, 6/7 slide it back (left/up) / forward (right/down). The defaults below are rushinput.DefaultMap's keyboard (rushhour_gym.human.DEFAULT_KEYS): LEFT/RIGHT and 3/4 choose, UP/DOWN and 1/2 (or , .) slide. Choosing calls no engine step; a slide becomes the engine's Discrete(32) action, logged as env_action (-1 for a choose). Keep the message Controls text in sync with 'keys' by hand.
_ergonomics_note: White triangles on the selected car show which of its two slides are legal (from the engine action_mask), because a refused move renders identically to a dropped keypress. 'movable_only' (default true, matching Rush-Hour's -movable-only default) makes selection skip cars that cannot move at all. false is Rush-Hour's -movable-only=false: a different task, since noticing which cars are stuck becomes part of the search -- keep it the same across sessions being compared.

text: Slide cars to free the RED car through
UP             slide it left, or up if vertical
DOWN           slide it right, or down if vertical
White triangles mark the moves a car can make.
